chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Salma, from Mu'ttab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The medical cures are four: the inhalation (sa'ut), the cupping (hijama), the hair removal (al-noura), and the enema (al-huqna).

key_terms.النُّورَةُ: Hair removal (specifically using a chemical paste)

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of medical cures mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies these four specific modalities—snuff (sa'ut), cupping (hijama), nit removal (nurah), and enema (huqna)—as the primary pillars of prophetic medicine, reflecting the holistic approach of the Ahl al-Bayt to physical health. This classification underscores the practical application of the principle that seeking cure is a form of worship and aligns with the Sunnah of the Prophet and his Imams in utilizing both natural remedies and procedural interventions for bodily purification.

en.hubeali: H 14674 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali, from Abu Salma, from Mo’tab, who has narrated: Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘
The medical cures are four – The inhalation, and the cupping, and the hair removal (Al-Noura), and the enema’.
